correction.text: 'the northern Tarim Basin from Turpan': Turpan, Yanqi (Karashahr), Kuqa and Aksu, the oases Mansur inherited

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: the Moghulistan row (1492-1511, 0.95 M km2 on the gazetteer, the whole Tarim and Turfan) is the nearest, but the Turpan page gives the khanate only the northern Tarim, and the south (Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan) belonged to the Dughlat emirate until Said Khan took Kashgar in 1514. This shape is 0.23 M km2. The Mansur page lists 'Yanqi, Bay, and Kuqa' with Turfan; Bay and the Aksu court are the page's, the radii are the researcher's reading.

correction.text: as 1487 plus Hami: 'Mansur fought the Ming again and took Kara Del in 1513'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Hami/Kara Del is the page's; whether Aksu stayed with Turpan after Said Khan's rise (1514-1516, Kashgar) is not dated by the pages opened, so it is kept to 1569. The Ming kept fighting over Hami in 1517, 1524 and 1528 (Mansur page).

region.text: the northern Tarim Basin from Turpan

ledger.note: 1487: Ahmad Alaq founds the Turpan Khanate. 'It was founded by Ahmad Alaq in 1487 based in Turpan as the eastern division of Moghulistan'; he 'gained independence from his brother Mahmud' and ruled the northern Tarim Basin.
1503: Mansur Khan becomes khan and holds court at Aksu. 'When he was nineteen, Mansur was made khan by his father'; he 'set up his court in Aksu'. The page has him ruling Turpan after 1516.

1513: Mansur takes Hami. 'Mansur fought the Ming again and took Kara Del in 1513'; the Mansur page: the Qara Del prince 'switched his allegiance from the Chinese Ming Emperor to Mansur Khan' that year and 'Turfan also annexed Hami'.
1516: the court is at Turpan. 'Peace was therefore made between the two brothers in 1516', with Mansur in Turfan and Said Khan in Kashgar; the page 'states he ruled Turpan after 1516'.

1517: the Ming fight Turpan over Hami. 'In 1517, 1524, and 1528 battles broke out'; in 1524 'Mansur tried to attack China in 1524 with 20,000 men, but was beaten by Chinese forces'. The page does not say who held Hami in each year.
1528: the last battle with the Ming that the page lists; no treaty is named and the page does not describe a Ming withdrawal from Hami ('Turfan also annexed Hami'). A bridging end.

1570: Yarkand conquers Turpan. 'In 1570, Abduraim Sultan of Khotan invaded. Muhammad Khan was captured, and Turpan came under Yarkand control.' The infobox end '1660?' and embassies to Beijing in 1647 and 1657 show a rump surviving as a Yarkand dependency.

wars.name: Hami campaign of 1513
wars.outcome: Mansur took Kara Del (Hami) in 1513 when its prince changed his allegiance from the Ming to Mansur.

wars.name: Ming–Turpan wars over Hami
wars.outcome: Battles in 1517, 1524 and 1528; Mansur was beaten by the Chinese in 1524 with 20,000 men. The page gives no treaty or border.

wars.name: Ahmad Alaq against the Shaybanids
wars.outcome: The Turpan page has Ahmad Alaq 'defeated and killed by Muhammad Shaybani' in the early 1500s; the Mansur page says 'both Ahmad and Mahmud were captured' in a failed campaign against the Uzbeks of Transoxiana. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Two pages disagree on whether Ahmad Alaq was killed or captured; the year is the page's 'early 1500s'.

wars.name: Yarkand conquest of Turpan
wars.outcome: Abduraim Sultan of Khotan invaded in 1570, captured Muhammad Khan and brought Turpan under Yarkand control.

certainty.note: Oasis frontiers between the Turpan, Aksu and Hami districts and the Ming guards are approximate; no line is recorded.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Turpan Khanate: the land sits inside the Moghulistan row (1492-1518, the whole Tarim and Turfan) and then Eastern Moghulistan (1519-1686, the Yarkent Khanate). The moghulistan dossier (ia-02-d) already flagged turpan-khanate as a missing counterpart. The rendering agents should draw Turpan, Karashahr, Kuqa, Aksu (and Hami from 1513) in this dossier's colour and the south Tarim (Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan) under the Dughlat emirate (to 1514) and then the Yarkent Khanate; the pages opened do not give the 1487-1514 south.

Dates: the infobox gives 1487 to '1660?', rulers 1487-1570 and then Muhammad Khan; this dossier ends at 1570 because the page says Turpan 'came under Yarkand control' then. Disagreements: Ahmad Alaq killed (Turpan page) or captured (Mansur page) by the Uzbeks; the Mansur page has the Hami prince switching allegiance in 1513 while the Turpan page has Mansur 'took' Kara Del. No page opened says how Hami passed back to the Ming, how long Turpan held it, or where the Ming frontier lay (the Jiayuguan line of 1524 is not on these pages). The Aksu court of 1503-1515 and Aksu after Said Khan's rise (1514) are not dated beyond the Mansur page.

Counterparts needing entries: kara-del (written in this batch), ming-dynasty (Hami battles 1517-1528), eastern-moghulistan (Yarkent Khanate, ia-03), moghulistan (the 1487 split, ia-02-d), dughlat-emirate (Kashgar-Yarkand-Khotan to 1514; flagged by ia-02-d).
